public_rationale: The observation holds. In August 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported that AT&T was saving up to 90% on some AI costs by using open models. It planned to raise their share from about 25% to 70-80% of its AI workloads. A report dated August 20 says AT&T was shifting large parts of its AI work away from Anthropic's models toward open models. In late July, AP reported that tokenmaxxing was 'hitting its limits' as costs rose, and that companies were routing work to cheaper models, including open-source ones. 'Collapse' is stronger than the reporting, which says the trend faded. The evidence for companies other than AT&T is general rather than specific. The forecast part of the sentence, that Anthropic's Q2 revenue 'may well not recur,' is hedged and is not graded here.
limitations: The AT&T details come from secondary summaries of the WSJ and The Information, not AT&T's own blog, which was unreadable.
AT&T still uses Claude for harder tasks and reportedly plans to hold its frontier-model spending flat, not cut it.
The hedged forecast about Anthropic's revenue is not graded here.

statement.excerpt: Indeed, THE big issue for Anthropic is that the kind of revenue they were making in the second quarter of this year may well not recur, at the same scale, next year, now that, in the aftermath of the collapse of tokenmaxxing, companies like ATT are increasingly turning to open source models from other vendors, in order to save costs.
statement.document_title: ARR vs ARR. Watch out for this one sly trick.

from_speaker: in the aftermath of the collapse of tokenmaxxing
are increasingly turning to open source models from other vendors
our_interpretation: The graded part is the present-tense observation: AT&T and similar companies were increasingly shifting AI work to open models from other vendors to cut costs, as the tokenmaxxing trend faded. The hedged forecast that Anthropic's Q2 revenue 'may well not recur' is not graded here.
'Collapse of tokenmaxxing' is read as the widely reported mid-2026 retreat from encouraging maximum token use, not a measured collapse in total spending.
'Increasingly' means a rising share of AI workloads moving to open models over the months before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Reports from around mid-2026 show AT&T moving a growing share of AI work to open models from other vendors, explicitly for cost savings, against a broader backdrop of companies pulling back from tokenmaxxing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports show AT&T was not shifting to open models, was not doing it for cost, or that tokenmaxxing had not faded.
